note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, price and opening time below comes from the City of Mesa's own pages: the Mesa Tennis & Pickleball Center's facility page, and the park pages for Kleinman and Chaparral. Six more Mesa parks say the words "Pickleball Court" without ever saying how many, and they are named in the local scene note rather than quietly left out.

slots.parking:
Mesa publishes nothing about parking at any of these three venues: no lot, no space count, no fee, no permit. What the City does publish is how you get in.

The Mesa Tennis & Pickleball Center is staffed, and asks you to "check-in at the front desk prior to your reservation to check-in and get your court assignment number". It warns that "Court fees must be paid inside pro shop before using the facility." Kleinman Park and Chaparral Park are ordinary municipal parks, open sunrise to 10 p.m., with no gate and no desk.
slots.peak_hours:
The Mesa Tennis & Pickleball Center closes in the middle of the day. Its published hours are 5:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. every day, then 5:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. Monday through Friday only. At the weekend it does not reopen in the evening at all.

The twenty-one courts are therefore open for about six hours on a weekday, a smaller window than the court count suggests. The City warns in its own words that "Tournaments, league and lesson programming, special events, or maintenance may limit court space for the general public". Kleinman and Chaparral are open sunrise to 10 p.m., and Mesa says nothing about when either is busy.
slots.surface_condition:
Mesa states a surface for none of these courts. What it does say about Chaparral Park is more useful than a surface note would be. The entry reads in full: "Pickleball Court (1 lined court shared with basketball use, bring your own portable net)".

One court, not several. Lines painted onto a basketball court, with the basketball use still there. And no net provided, which is the most practical fact on this page. The Center's twenty-one courts are described by the City only as "lighted pickleball courts". Kleinman says least of all: four courts, counted, and no description of them.
slots.local_scene:
Twenty-six courts at three venues, and twenty-one of them are in one place. The Mesa Tennis & Pickleball Center holds one of the largest single-venue pickleball counts in this directory. It is staffed and floodlit, with a pro shop and ball machines for hire, and play costs $9.00 per court per hour before 5 p.m. and $13.00 after.

Then there is a long tail. Mesa's parks pages carry the words "Pickleball Court" at six more parks (Gene Autry, Christopher J. Brady, Red Mountain, Augusta Ranch, Sheepherders and Washington) and not one of them states a number. Red Mountain and Augusta Ranch have lines on a basketball court and ask you to bring a net. People plainly play at all six. The real number of pickleball courts in Mesa is comfortably higher than twenty-six, and this page will not guess how much higher.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a real game on a proper court
best_for.text: The Mesa Tennis & Pickleball Center has twenty-one lighted pickleball courts, one of the largest counts at any single venue on this site. It is staffed, it has a pro shop and ball machines to rent, and you can book a court online up to a fortnight ahead. It also costs money and keeps unusual hours: $9.00 per court per hour before 5 p.m., $13.00 after, open mornings 5:30 to 11:30 every day and evenings 5:00 to 10:00 on weekdays only.

best_for.heading: Best if you just want to turn up
best_for.text: Kleinman Park has four pickleball courts in a park that is open sunrise to 10 p.m., with restrooms, ramadas and a softball complex on the same site. The City states no charge for the courts, though it does not state that they are free either. Courts here are booked through the Tennis & Pickleball Center if you want one reserved.

best_for.heading: Best only if you own a net
best_for.text: Chaparral Park is one court, and the City is unusually honest about what that means: lines on a basketball court, shared with basketball, and no net provided. If you have a portable net in the boot this is a perfectly good hit close to central Mesa. If you do not, it is not a pickleball court that day.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Mesa have?
faqs.a: Twenty-six, across three venues: twenty-one at the Mesa Tennis & Pickleball Center, four at Kleinman Park and one at Chaparral Park. Six further Mesa parks list pickleball courts without stating a number, so the true figure is higher and the City has not published it.

faqs.q: Which Mesa venue has the most courts?
faqs.a: The Mesa Tennis & Pickleball Center, at 4125 E McKellips Rd, with twenty-one lighted pickleball courts. That is one of the largest single-venue counts anywhere in this directory.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Mesa?
faqs.a: Not at the Center, which charges $9.00 per court per hour before 5 p.m. and $13.00 after, and states that fees must be paid at the pro shop first. At Kleinman and Chaparral the City publishes no price at all, which is not the same as publishing that they are free.

faqs.q: Are these courts indoor or outdoor?
faqs.a: Mesa never states it, at any of the three venues.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: At Chaparral Park, yes. The City says so: "bring your own portable net". At the Center, no; it is a full facility with permanent courts. At Kleinman the City does not say.

At the Center, yes, online up to two weeks ahead. Kleinman Park's courts are also reservable, and the City directs those bookings through the Tennis & Pickleball Center. Chaparral is not listed as reservable.
